Chapter 8: Sustaining Motivation and Avoiding Burnout.
Let’s be honest—chasing originality is exciting, but it can really take it out of you. It’s not just about being passionate. To keep going, you need resilience, self-care, and a deeper purpose—something bigger than just the project in front of you.
If you’re someone who likes to think outside the box, you’ve probably hit your fair share of setbacks, heard some doubts, or felt like things were moving at a snail’s pace. So, how do you keep from burning out? Well, original thinkers often develop habits that help them recharge and keep things in perspective.
First, connect to a deeper purpose. Remind yourself why your work matters—not just what you hope to achieve right now, but the bigger mission behind it all. That sense of meaning can really pull you through the tough moments.
Next, set some boundaries. This one’s huge. Make sure you’re carving out time for rest, for relationships, and for the things that lift you up. When your mind gets a chance to wander and recharge, that’s when creativity really starts to flow.
And don’t forget to celebrate progress, not just the end results. Every small win, every little step forward—it all counts. Don’t wait for that big breakthrough to pat yourself on the back.
Just think about a social entrepreneur who’s trying to change education. She might face years of resistance and red tape. But by focusing on the difference she’s making for even one student, she finds the energy to keep going, without feeling crushed by the size of the challenge.
It’s also crucial to notice when burnout is creeping in. If you’re feeling constantly drained, getting cynical, or doubting your own effectiveness, it might be time to reach out for support. Remember, originality isn’t a sprint—it’s a marathon. The people who stick with it? They’re usually the ones who pace themselves and lean on their communities when they need to.
So, here’s the key takeaway: to keep your originality alive, you’ve got to look after both your mind and your spirit. By staying connected to your purpose, setting healthy boundaries, and celebrating each bit of progress, you can keep your energy and resilience strong—no matter how long the journey gets.
